system.description:
This Charm reverses its prerequisite, so an object goes from the Sidereal to someone or someplace else. The Sidereal may set any object on its way with this Charm, not only those she creates, needing only the name of the place or person. She cannot target attuned artifacts, and this can be dealt with as a Shaping effect when targeting other objects. While setting the object on its way, she knots its destiny to the fate of a chosen person or location. The destiny-guided object moves toward its goal for as long as the Sidereal keeps Essence committed to the Charm. This may take less than a day for a person in the same town, or many months to cross Creation. Each week, the Sidereal's player rolls (Wits + [Craft necessary to create the object]), adding (Craft [Fate]) bonus dice. The Exalt may apply Excellencies normally to each roll. A botch on any of these rolls indicates the object was destroyed or otherwise cannot proceed any further. The character knows when this happens or when the object finally reaches its destination. The object sent by this Charm may simply be useful in its own right—or dangerous, such as a forged map designed to lure the target into a trap. It can also carry a Sidereal astrology effect as part of the object's fate-crafting, as a way to deliver ascending or descending destinies to people or places the Sidereal cannot reach directly.

The Storyteller sets a cumulative difficulty based on both distance and probability, which may range as high as 50. The cumulative difficulty for an object journeying within the same realm of existence should rarely exceed 20, and for traveling between realms of existence it should rarely be less than 30. The difficulty for each roll is the same as the per-roll difficulty to Craft the object. The Charm ends prematurely only if the Exalt rolls more than (Essence) botches in a row.

At Craft and Essence 5+ a Sidereal may use this Charm to banish things from a realm of existence rather than sending them somewhere specific. Once such an object passes beyond the bounds of the originating realm, it becomes lost to that world—the destiny tangled about it will not permit it to return. For every dot of Essence the Sidereal possesses, either a botch will occur on an action necessary to return the item, or some new circumstance will arise to prevent or redirect its return.

The instant before he dies, a Vizier may empower his banishments to persist past his ending. At that time, he chooses which banishments he currently maintains that will continue and which to release normally. Thereafter, the effect cannot be undone without ablating the protective destinies that keep the object away.
